Golem. Standing in the south corner is an iron golem that looks like a 10-foot-tall duergar. The golem understands Dwarvish and obeys Valtagar’s commands.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 16. Fire and Iron; 16a. Northern Smelter
text: Smiths. Two sweaty, unarmored duergar are working the forge, smelting iron. Both wear tinted goggles and thick gloves.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 16. Fire and Iron; 16a. Northern Smelter
text: The forge puts out tremendous heat thanks to a fire elemental magically trapped inside it. Runes carved on the inside walls of the forge prevent the elemental from escaping or harming anyone outside the forge. Destroying the forge releases the elemental, whereupon it attacks everyone in sight. The forge has AC 17, 80 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 16. Fire and Iron; 16b. Southern Smelter
text: This room is identical to area 16a except that the forge protrudes from the south wall, and the two unarmored duergar working here are a pair of females named Krinxa and Wolthra.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 16. Fire and Iron; 16c. Iron Stockpile
text: Duergar. In the north half of the room, an elderly male duergar carrying an iron cane and an ear horn sits in a stone rocking chair next to a pile of iron molds and clamps.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 16. Fire and Iron; 16d. Barracks
text: This room contains two dozen iron cots arranged haphazardly in the middle of the space. Ten duergar, five males and five females, are asleep here at any given time, snoring loudly. The males are named Bulborm, Daarsh, Krod, Mranhaim, and Muzdrok. The females are named Azgra, Narlith, Roxinda, Sorka, and Svilla.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 17. Hammers and Anvils; 17a. Western Guard Post
text: Two male duergar, Kalrog and Klang, keep guard here. Klang is Kalrog’s older brother, and the two are highly competitive.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 17. Hammers and Anvils; 17b. Eastern Guard Post
text: Smoke and heat from the forges billow into this chamber, keeping it a sweltering 90 degrees Fahrenheit. Two duergar — a male named Prax and a female named Torga — mind this watch post, incidentally standing guard over a variety of extra supplies that are stored here. Driven into the south wall are twelve stone pegs on which soot-stained leather aprons and tinted goggles are hung.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 17. Hammers and Anvils; 17c. Western Smithy
text: Smiths. Two sweaty, female duergar are fashioning an iron javelin. Both are unarmored, wearing leather aprons and gloves. One of them wears tinted iron goggles as she hammers the javelin into shape. The other has an iron eye patch and uses tongs to hold the metal in place as it’s struck.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 17. Hammers and Anvils; 17d. Eastern Smithy
text: This room is identical to area 17c except that the two unarmored duergar working here are males named Forn and Wulluk, and they’re fashioning shields and bits of scale mail instead of weapons. Forn is fat and lazy, Wulluk old and cantankerous. They grate on each other’s nerves and constantly put each other down. They otherwise behave similarly to the duergar in area 17c.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 18. Iron Mine; 18b. Duergar Miners
text: Seven duergar — three males named Greorx, Hwahl, and Uzwurn, and four females named Awmok, Nezza, Proxna, and Warda — mine iron ore here. Eager for any distraction, the miners attack intruders on sight. Given the noise that echoes throughout the tunnels, the sound of clashing steel is unlikely to be noticed by the duergar in areas 18c and 18d. Magical explosions or other unusual sounds do draw their attention, though.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 18. Iron Mine; 18c. A Miner Disturbance
text: Eleven duergar work here. Three of the workers are enlarged female duergar (Brakka, Korla, and Zagra) who use picks to break up a vein of iron ore that runs through the ceiling. Six normal-sized males (Hax, Mruuzdain, Oznur, Ramdrax, Tarnvur, and Yarox) work on expanding the cavern northward, while two normal-sized females (Nura and Speleosa) use hammers and spikes to separate iron from loose chunks of rock. If the miners notice the party, they attack, letting their enlarged allies barrel in first.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 18. Iron Mine; 18d. Overseer
text:
Stalagma. Stalagma Steelshadow, a female adult steel dragon in duergar form, is mounted on a gorgon near the bend in the mine track. (If Valtagar Steelshadow escaped from area 15, he is riding behind Stalagma on the gorgon.)
Xorn. Three xorn under Stalagma’s command are gathered around a broken mine cart filled with coins.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 19. Outpost; 19a. Way to Level 22
text: Xindulus. An invisible ultroloth named Xindulus guards a secret door leading to a 10-foot-wide spiral staircase that descends to level 22 (see “Secret Door” below).

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 19. Outpost; 19a. Way to Level 22
text: If anyone opens the secret door, the ultroloth appears and tries to slay them. It ignores those who leave the secret door alone, allowing them to move through the area unmolested. If threatened by three or more enemies, it tries to summon 1d6 mezzoloths, 1d4 nycaloths, or another ultroloth (see the “Variant: Yugoloth Summoning” sidebar in the “Yugoloths” entry in the Monster Manual).

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 20. Poisonous Mine; 20b. Poisoned Miners
text: Three poisoned duergar (two males and one female) use picks to chip iron ore from the walls of this cave. If outnumbered, they turn invisible and join their fellows in area 20c. Otherwise, they attack. The males are named Orn and Thumrok. The female is named Durundra.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 20. Poisonous Mine; 20c. Poisoned Miners
text: Eight poisoned duergar (six males and two females) lethargically swing their picks, working iron veins in the cavern walls. They are hostile toward non-duergar. They’re bold if they outnumber their foes but flee to area 21 if that situation changes. The males are named Hrok, Jarazk, Krod, Mraginar, Norl, and Rok. The females are named Bralith and Sunmerva.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 23. Fazrian’s Court; 23b. Hall of Final Judgment
text: Fazrian and Fiend. A hairless, green-skinned planetar with white-feathered wings and eyes of molten silver sits on a bone throne in a raised alcove. Lurking in the shadows behind the throne is Raxxus, a nycaloth. (The yugoloth passively guards the wall behind it, which contains a secret door to area 24.)

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 23. Fazrian’s Court; 23b. Hall of Final Judgment
text: Standing Gate. To the north stands a pair of crystal menhirs, each imprisoning a marilith.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 23. Fazrian’s Court; 23b. Hall of Final Judgment
text: Fazrian is a lawful evil planetar that lacks the Healing Touch action option. Unless he is incapacitated, Fazrian can take one of the following lair actions on initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties) while on the Terminus Level:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Terminus Level; Exploring This Level; 23. Fazrian’s Court; 23c. Garbage Disposal
text: At the end of the tunnel lurk three hungry otyughs. When they detect other creatures in the pit, they rush forth and attack while using their Limited Telepathy to taunt prey.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 1. Grand Foyer
text: Grells. Six grells float behind the pillars to the north. The grells attack visitors and can use their tentacles to open and close doors as needed.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 3. West Wing
text: Four nothics lurk in the northern arm of this L-shaped gallery, poring over wall carvings and chattering to themselves. Beyond the nothics, a staircase descends 50 feet to tier 2.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 4. Decayed Quarters; 4a. Grell Nest
text: A hive-like nest with multiple dark openings fills the southern half of this room. Seven grells lurk inside the wet, papery nest and emerge from it to attack intruders.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 4. Decayed Quarters; 4b. Mad Creature
text: Nothic. A nothic squats near the east wall, frantically scratching at the stone.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 6. Kitchen
text: Unseen Servants. Four living unseen servants (see appendix A) prepare meals on command and use brooms to sweep the floor.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 8. Nothic’s Niche
text: Fissure. A nothic hides in a 5-foot-wide natural fissure in the 20-foot-high ceiling.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 9. East Wing
text: Drifting Light. A visible will-o’-wisp drifts through this long, L-shaped gallery.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 10. Noble Quarters
text: This suite belongs to Melissara Shadowdusk, a distant cousin of the Shadowdusk twins, and her deranged husband, Derrion.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 10. Noble Quarters; 10a. Melissara’s Chamber
text: Melissara. A middle-aged woman (Melissara Shadowdusk) sits in an easy chair in the northeast corner, reading and muttering to herself.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 10. Noble Quarters; 10b. Derrion’s Chamber
text: Derrion. A middle-aged man with a scarred face (Derrion Shadowdusk) is pacing about the room anxiously.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 1; 13. Walking Dead
text: Zombie. A human zombie in rotting, soiled robes shuffles back and forth through the room. A powerful stench of decay accompanies it.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 16. Arcane Sanctum
text: Three invisible will-o’-wisps linger in this area in case Vertrand or Berlain require their services.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 17. Vertrand’s Room
text: Vertrand. A bald, elderly man (Vertrand Shadowdusk) sits at a writing desk to the north, his back to the doorway.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 18. Berlain’s Suite; 18b. Bedchamber
text: Monsters. A mutated humanoid (Berlain Shadowdusk) sits on the edge of the bed, patching gashes in her robe. Floating nearby are two grells.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 20. Pillared Hall; 20a. Central Chamber
text:
Guards. Five invisible will-o’-wisps patrol this area.
Five nothics hide behind the pillars in this area. They fight alongside the will-o’-wisps in area 20a but avoid combat otherwise. If the characters attack the nothics, any will-o’-wisps in area 20a come to the nothics’ aid.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 24. Nothic Warrens; 24a. Communal Area
text: Twelve nothics gather here and glare suspiciously at strangers while spouting nonsense among themselves. If the characters do anything to startle the nothics, they attack; otherwise, the nothics let characters pass through this room unmolested.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 24. Nothic Warrens; 24b. Peek-a-Boo
text: Two nothics cower beneath mounds of rotting tapestries piled against the east wall. The nothics sheepishly observe passersby and avoid combat.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 2; 28. Legacy of Xerrion
text: Slaadi. Four invisible death slaadi stand guard next to the northernmost pillars. The slaadi serve at the pleasure of Dezmyr and Zalthar, and they attack intruders on sight.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 3; 31. Approach to Madness; 31b. Threshold of Insanity
text: Slaadi. Four invisible death slaadi stand in front of the double door leading to area 32. The slaadi serve at the pleasure of Dezmyr and Zalthar, and they attack intruders on sight.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 3; 34. Zalthar’s Chambers; 34a. Zalthar Shadowdusk
text: Zalthar. Seated in a chair, facing the northern and western doors, is Zalthar Shadowdusk — a death knight in black armor. In his withered hands, he holds two tiny painted wooden figurines (busts of himself and his sister as young children, which he took from the fresco in area 19).

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 3; 34. Zalthar’s Chambers; 34b. Black Obelisk
text: Characters who have a combined Strength of 60 or higher can topple the obelisk, which is a Huge object with AC 17, 90 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. Toppling or destroying the obelisk releases a couatl trapped within. The couatl, named Tezca-Zyanya, appears in the form of a Tiny yellow frog. Using its telepathy, the disguised couatl thanks the characters for releasing it. Exposure to the Far Realm has deprived the couatl of its memories, including those that would explain its entrapment and the purpose of the obelisk.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 3; 38. Dezmyr’s Chambers; 38c. Dezmyr’s Sanctum
text: Dezmyr. Dezmyr Shadowdusk (see below) stands in the middle of the room, clad in ancient armor and joined by six wraiths (her counselors).

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 3; 39. Dracolich’s Phylactery
text: Cassiok and Pet. Facing the statue with its back to the rest of the room is a black-robed creature (Cassiok Shadowdusk) leaning heavily on a staff. Next to Cassiok is his loyal pet, a grick alpha, and an invisible gray slaad that serves as his valet.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Shadowdusk Hold; Tier 3; 40. Lynnorax’s Lair
text: Dracolich. Lynnorax, an adult blue dracolich, faces the double door to the east and exhales lightning in that direction as soon as it sees intruders.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 4. Helmed Horrors
text: Six helmed horrors float in the alcoves marked H on map 23. These constructs attack intruders on sight and fly after those who flee.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 5. Magical Repository
text: Dome. A deep, 20-foot-high alcove in the north wall contains four invisible stalkers trapped inside an invisible, dome-shaped wall of force rising from the floor. (Any items that Halaster removed from the mine carts in level 15, area 1, lie on the floor inside the dome. The dome appears to contain nothing else.)

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 6. Wizardly Wards; 6b. Angelic Shield
text: A detect magic spell reveals an aura of abjuration magic around the otherwise ordinary shield, inside which is trapped a pit fiend named Kastzanedes. Any ability that detects the presence of fiends, such as a paladin’s Divine Sense class feature, reveals the presence of such a creature bound within the shield.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 9. Vaults; 9b. Diabolical Shield
text: A detect magic spell reveals an aura of abjuration magic around the otherwise ordinary shield, inside which is trapped a deva named Aryx. While trapped in the shield, Aryx can’t communicate with anyone. Any ability that detects the presence of celestials, such as a paladin’s Divine Sense class feature, reveals the presence of such a creature bound within the shield. If a dispel evil and good spell is cast on the shield, or if the shield comes within 10 feet of a fiend, the deva is released, appearing within 5 feet of the shield or in the nearest unoccupied space. Once freed, the deva uses its detect evil and good spell to determine if there are any evil creatures in its presence. If so, Aryx attacks them, targeting fiends above all others.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 10. Arcane Display; 10a. Zigzagging Gallery
text: Characters who make a loud racket in this hall attract the seven flameskulls in area 10b. The features of this hall are as follows:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 10. Arcane Display; 10b. Shield Trap
text: Flameskulls. Unless they were drawn to area 10a, seven flameskulls float here, their green flames the only sources of light in this room.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 11. Trobriand’s Workshop; 11b. Scaladar
text: Guards. Two scaladar (see appendix A) guard this room and won’t leave it under any circumstances.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 13. The Metal Mage
text: Trobriand is looking forward to testing his new body and attacks intruders on sight, showing no mercy.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 13. The Metal Mage; Trobriand
text: Deactivating or destroying one or more of the pillars, destroying the golem, or forcing the golem out of the room causes Trobriand’s spirit to vacate the golem and attempt to reunite with his normal body, which is hidden in area 11c. If the characters have not destroyed his body, Trobriand’s spirit returns to it immediately, and he awakens in area 11c as an archmage with the same spell list as in his golem form and the same spell slots remaining as he had when he left his golem body. His primary goal thereafter is to destroy the characters for meddling in his affairs.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 13. The Metal Mage; Trobriand
text: If the golem in this room has not been destroyed when Trobriand’s spirit leaves it, the golem becomes an ordinary iron golem under the Metal Mage’s command and attacks intruders on sight.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 14. Man with the Rabbit’s Head
text: A short, plump, rabbit-headed man wearing a dirty servant’s uniform cowers in the square marked X on map 23. “Rabbithead” is a commoner, with these changes:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 17. Arcturia’s Court
text:
Arcturia. Arcturia — a gaunt figure with blue scales, bone spurs on her forearms and elbows, gossamer wings, and a flowing gown — dances to music atop a stepped dais 5 feet higher than the rest of the room.
Furnishings. Arranged throughout the hall are four stuffed chairs, four padded footstools, two divans, and two large coffee tables. (These furnishings are twelve mimics in disguise. Arcturia considers them her most trusted friends. If the lich comes under attack or takes umbrage with visitors, the mimics are quick to reveal their true forms and fight alongside her.)
The three humanoids wearing armor are champions (see appendix A) with the heads of a dingo, an iguana, and a stork. If Arcturia becomes embroiled in a battle, two of them fight on her side. The one with the dingo head, who secretly despises Arcturia, sides with her enemies against her. Each guard carries a yellow sapphire (see “Treasure” below).
The three servants are unarmed commoners with the heads of an aardvark, a moth, and a shrew. Whenever Arcturia snaps her fingers and points to a spot in the room, these servants begin dusting that location and don’t stop until she snaps her fingers again. They otherwise avoid combat.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 20. Hidden Helm
text: Sensors. Near the ceiling float four invisible scrying sensors created by the four ultroloths in area 21a using clairvoyance spells. If the ultroloths spot intruders in the room, they teleport to this location and attack.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; The Dungeon; 21. Displaced Vault; 21a. Acid and Glass
text: Ultroloths. Four ultroloths (each marked with a U on map 23) lurk in alcoves along the north and south walls of this 30-foot-high room.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 24. Potion Brewery
text: Demilich. Floating behind the table is a demilich that looks like a human skull with a jagged crack that extends above and below one eye socket.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 25. Factory
text: Unseen Servants. Six living unseen servants (see appendix A) are gathered around two wooden tables, where they are using mortars and pestles to grind dead beetles into ink, and wooden frames and stone scrapers to stretch and scrape leather to create sheets of parchment. The servants ignore visitors.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 31. Art Studio
text: Eight living unseen servants (see appendix A) are painting four new portraits of Halaster and carving a statue of him in this room. Characters who enter the room see the following features:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 33. Mad Mage Showdown
text: Magic Circle. Inscribed on the floor in the middle of the room is a 40-foot-diameter circle of glowing runes. Halaster uses it to summon an empyrean who owes him a favor. (The circle serves no other purpose.)

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 33. Mad Mage Showdown
text: If the characters took any actions to hinder Halaster/u2019s current goal, the Mad Mage expresses his displeasure and attacks them.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 35. Exercise Room
text: Golems. Two flesh golems are working out in this room. One golem is doing shoulder shrugs with two 100-pound iron kettlebells. The other switches back and forth between jumping jacks and shadowboxing.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Mad Wizard’s Lair; Halaster’s Tower; 36. Gate to Triboar
text: This room contains a pair of 15-foot-tall standing stones. Lashed to each stone with 50 feet of hempen rope is an inanimate scarecrow, like the ones found in farmers’ fields. Perched atop the northernmost standing stone is an ordinary crow (use the raven statistics). The crow caws at anyone who enters the room and bonds with a random character.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Skullport Overview; What Dwells Here?; Flameskulls
text: Thirteen ancient flameskulls haunt Skullport. These entities, which have defended the town since its founding, are all that remain of the Sargauth Enclave, a settlement of Netherese wizards. The flameskulls consider themselves the true rulers of Skullport, but they have lost touch with reality, their minds drifting in and out of the present and the past. They rarely communicate, and when they do it is often in a dead language.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring Skull Island; 4. Duergar Barracks
text: Ten duergar are quartered in this two-story building.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring Skull Island; 5. Human Barracks
text: This three-story edifice looms over the northeast harbor (area 3b). Seventy human thugs are quartered here.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring Skull Island; 7. Bugbear Barracks
text: Sixty bugbears inhabit this two-story stone building.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring Skull Island; 8. Gargoyle Towers
text: Twelve gargoyles perch on the battlements of these three-story stone towers (four atop each tower).

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring Skull Island; 9. Tower of the Seven Woes
text: The fortress’s half-ogre commander, Sundeth, lives in this hollowed-out spire with his wyvern mount. Sundeth is a hideous, 8-foot-tall, half-ogre champion (see appendix A), with these changes:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring Skull Island; 10. Kuo-toa Lair; 10b. Kuo-toa Cave
text: A hungry kuo-toa named Hlool crouches in the middle of this cave. If the characters give it food, Hlool eats the food, then dives to the bottom of the River Sargauth, returns minutes later with a bundled-up cloak of the manta ray that it took from a dead adventurer, and gives it to the characters as a thank-you gift.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 12. Dead Man’s Corner
text:
A sea hag named Olive Stillwater sells human zombies out of this dilapidated shop. She appears as an old woman covered with snails and barnacles.
Olive keeps a dozen human zombies in her cramped shop. “They’re great for setting off traps!” she says with a chuckle. As payment for each zombie, she demands a tiny vial of the buyer’s blood and three hairs plucked from the buyer’s head. She owns a pair of rusty iron shears that can be used to draw blood and cut hair. After consuming this payment, Olive gains the innate ability to cast the animate dead spell once per day for the next three days.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 15. The Black Tankard
text: The proprietor of this squalid, one-story tavern is a fat, dour duergar named Droon Stonedark, who works for Xanathar. Two minotaurs stand in dark corners, ready to give unruly patrons the heave-ho. A spectator floats amid the rafters and provides additional security.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 20. Dark Harvest Market
text: Food harvested from the Underdark is sold here by 1d6 duergar, who employ an equal number of wererats as bodyguards.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 24. Thaglar’s Foundry
text: Skullport’s ugly stone foundry stands four stories tall. Inside, duergar smiths under the command of a brutal duergar taskmaster named Thaglar Xundorn fashion weapons, armor, and tools.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 26. The Keel Hall
text: Bosskyn Gorrb, a blind tiefling spy, leads the Zhentarim in Skullport and uses flying snakes to deliver messages to his underlings. If one or more characters are members of the Zhentarim and can prove it, Bosskyn offers to help them in one or both of the following ways:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 27. The Poisoned Quill
text: “Tas” is an elderly archmage. Her secret is that she and Halaster are friends. The Mad Mage visits her about once a month for tea, and she catches him up on the latest news and gossip. When they are together, Halaster and Tasselgryn act like an old married couple.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 31. Dalagor’s Fortress
text: Felrax, a dragonborn mage with copper-colored scales, watches over the mansion. A light cantrip cast on his staff allows Felrax to see in the dark interior. If one or more characters are Harpers, Felrax offers to help them in one or both of the following ways:

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 32. Dumathoin’s Jest
text: Ygarra Urmbaalt, a duergar, appraises gemstones for a flat fee of 20 percent of a gem’s value. Her establishment is a one-story, ugly stone building.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 33. The Overflowing Urn
text: Five years ago, a doppelganger killed Garryth and assumed his identity after disposing of the body. The doppelganger is content running the business and has no qualms about paying money to Xanathar for protection.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 34. Nightshade’s Caress
text: Displayed in the window of this shop are various herbs, elixirs, vials of poison, and baskets of medicinal fungi. The store is cluttered with more such goods, all labeled and clearly priced. The apothecary, Nightshade, is an undead creature (use the mummy statistics) that looks like a withered crone dressed in a tattered black robe.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 35. The Worm’s Gullet
text: The only restaurant in town is located inside a petrified, hollowed-out purple worm. The food and the service have gone downhill ever since Xanathar installed a new manager: a heartless duergar named Gharz Stonedark.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 35. The Worm’s Gullet
text: Gharz makes meals out of whatever his kobolds can find, and patrons are expected to eat whatever Gharz serves them. Common meals include stirge loaf, carrion crawler soufflé, flumph stew, and hot shrieker pie. The house ale is Wyrmwizz, straight from the local distillery (area 16). A meal with a drink costs 5 sp per person.

book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage
book_path: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage; Skullport; Exploring the Town; 36. Tanor’thal Refuge
text: Carved by the drow of House Tanor’thal, this stronghold resembles an upside-down spider that looms above the rest of Skullport like a great, dark god. The spider’s hollowed-out head, thorax, and abdomen contain windowless living quarters filled with thick webs and a host of giant spiders. Other denizens of Skullport avoid this place, making it an excellent refuge once the spiders are cleared out. The drow left nothing of value behind when they vacated their refuge.
